submitter: bugs_open/283 session (RFC_032 step 1, ROUND 2 — response to round 1's objections)
rationale:
ROUND 2 on the same correlation. Round 1 (pass 0: swap the retired {{.ComponentID}} for {{.InstanceID}} before the brace-excluding harvest) was APPROVED with three advisory objections, none high. This round is the response to them, plus ONE defect of my own that answering them exposed — which is why it is a new round rather than a trailer on the approved one: it adds a new REFUSAL CLASS on a shared seam, and round 1 reviewed no such thing.

THE DEFECT ROUND 1 FOUND, stated first because it is the substance. bug_historian (edit 4) and guardian (edit 1) independently objected that pass 0 lives in ConvertTemplateToInstanceScope, which ScopeToolBirthTemplate calls, so BOTH ARMED BIRTH GUARDS (create_tool_component, deploy_tool_to_site, live since v1.0.1322) inherited a live behaviour change that only the converter's own tests exercised. bug_historian put the risk conditionally: 'if the birth-guard path has any code that treated the old refusal as an expected outcome, that path is now silently bypassed'. I RAN THE CENSUS INSTEAD OF LEAVING IT CONDITIONAL (grep -rn RefusedReason over *.go): exactly ONE production consumer keys on the refusal TEXT — tool_birth_instance_scope.go:111, `case strings.Contains(rep.RefusedReason, "declares no literal element ids")`, which returns the caller's bytes VERBATIM in both armed and unarmed mode. So the conditional is real, and it is worse than the seats could see from the plan: a template with NO literal ids that carries {{.ComponentID}} where pass 0 cannot rewrite it (a data-* value, a #selector, a script literal, or the mismatched-quote attribute the fix below now declines) reaches that SAME early return, takes that arm, and is persisted verbatim under the comment 'nothing to collide on' — which is the opposite of the truth, because the placeholder renders the SAME value on every instance. That is the collision this whole seam exists to remove, arriving through the guard built to stop it. Round 1's own test for the placeholder-outside-an-id-attribute case does not catch it: all three of its fixtures carry a literal id="wrap", so they never reach the empty-harvest return.

THE FIX IS TWO GUARDS IN SERIES, and the mutation runs show each is independently necessary: (1) the refusal reason now NAMES the placeholder when one survives an empty harvest, and (2) the birth guard's inert-safe arm excludes any reason naming ComponentID. Reverting either one alone puts the template back on the pass-through path — measured, both mutations fail the same call-site test with the same message.

THE OTHER OBJECTIONS. editquality edit 3 / bug_historian edit 1 (both low) asked for a backreference so the closing quote must match the opening one: `(["'])...\2`. THAT CANNOT BE WRITTEN IN THIS ENGINE — Go's regexp is RE2, which has no backreferences. The pairing is therefore enforced in the replace function (g[2] != g[3] declines the rewrite), and the comment records why the suggested form is unavailable so the next reader does not try it. Declining rather than rewriting is deliberate: rewriting would launder a malformed attribute the browser never parsed as an id into a well-formed one, and the template then falls to the completeness refusal, which is the fail-loud direction this file states. editquality's 'missing' item — that reElementID's brace exclusion is cited as grounding but not patched — is now named IN THE CODE as a deliberate deferral with its reason (a detector fix has its own blast radius across every DetectInstanceCollisions caller; it belongs in RFC_032's track, not riding in on a converter change). guardian edit 4 asked whether a new report key could surprise a consumer keyed on exact field sets: censused — InstanceConversionReport is NEVER whole-marshalled, every consumer hand-builds its key list (fix_component_template_action.go:1306,1337), so it is additive-safe. The same census showed TemplatedIDSwaps was written and READ BY NOBODY, so this round surfaces it in the fixer's result map and the birth guard's info — it matters because on the five section templates it is the ONLY non-zero counter the conversion produces, so without it a successful conversion is indistinguishable at the work-item result from one that did nothing. guardian edit 2 asked for a doc_note on the new refusal class: it is going into LANDMINES.md, which is the estate's system of record and syncs into doc_notes.

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS ROUND, deliberately. The five templates are still not converted and nothing is re-rendered; 18 live pages still serve duplicate section ids and 11 serve id="" (as of 2026-08-22). Separately, and NOT fixed here: two of the four render paths (RenderComponentAction, the section editor) bind the token via BindSingleSectionInstanceToken, which supplies occurrence 0 — correct only while a component appears once per page, which is exactly what these five templates violate. Converting them fixes the full-page paths that serve the pages and leaves those two single-section paths writing a colliding-but-detectable token. That is RFC_032's next step and is being filed as such, not silently absorbed here.

plan.summary: Round 2 of the RFC_032 pass-0 change, responding to round 1's three advisory objections. Two guards in series close a hole the approved plan did not see: a template with no literal ids carrying {{.ComponentID}} outside an id attribute was routed, by refusal-reason TEXT, into the birth guard's inert-safe arm and persisted verbatim on both armed guards. Plus: RE2 has no backreferences, so the quote pairing the seats asked for is enforced in the replace function; the deferred detector fix is named in the code; and the report counter that nothing read is surfaced where the conversion's only non-zero evidence lives.

edits.rationale: Two changes. (a) Quote pairing enforced in the replace func because RE2 has no backreference; a mismatched pair declines the rewrite and falls through to the completeness refusal rather than being laundered into a well-formed attribute. (b) The empty-harvest early return now distinguishes 'no ids at all' (inert, pass-through correct) from 'no literal ids but the retired placeholder survives somewhere pass 0 cannot rewrite' (NOT inert — same value on every instance). The reason string is load-bearing because one production caller routes on its text. Also names the reElementID deferral per editquality.

diff --git a/platform/orchestration/actions/component_instance_conversion.go b/platform/orchestration/actions/component_instance_conversion.go
index 1565e7bfb..9c6192b67 100644
--- a/platform/orchestration/actions/component_instance_conversion.go
+++ b/platform/orchestration/actions/component_instance_conversion.go
@@ -53,8 +53,16 @@
 // per-instance placeholder. Deliberately tolerant of Go template whitespace and
 // trim markers ({{- .ComponentID -}}), because the corpus is LLM-written and a
 // spelling this misses would be silently left behind rather than loudly
-// refused. Group 1 is the leading whitespace, group 2 the quote character, so
-// the rewrite preserves both.
+// refused. Group 1 is the leading whitespace, group 2 the OPENING quote and
+// group 3 the CLOSING one, so the rewrite preserves the first and the caller
+// can compare the pair.
+//
+// ⚠ The two quotes are separate groups because Go's regexp is RE2, which has
+// NO BACKREFERENCES — `\3` cannot be written here to force the closing quote to
+// match the opening one (council round 1 on this change, editquality/edit 3 and
+// bug_historian/edit 1, both suggested exactly that). The pairing is therefore
+// enforced in the replace function below, where a mismatched pair declines the
+// rewrite instead of emitting `id="…'`.
 var reComponentIDInIDAttr = regexp.MustCompile(`(\s)id=(["'])\{\{-?\s*\.ComponentID\s*-?\}\}(["'])`)
 
 // reComponentIDAnywhere — the same placeholder in ANY position, for the
@@ -138,8 +146,18 @@ func ConvertTemplateToInstanceScope(tpl string) (string, InstanceConversionRepor
 	// id IS the instance's identity rather than an id scoped WITHIN it, and
 	// the prefix form would render `c-faq-` with nothing after the hyphen.
 	swapped := reComponentIDInIDAttr.ReplaceAllStringFunc(tpl, func(m string) string {
-		rep.TemplatedIDSwaps++
 		g := reComponentIDInIDAttr.FindStringSubmatch(m)
+		if g[2] != g[3] {
+			// Mismatched quotes (id="{{.ComponentID}}'). Not a well-formed
+			// attribute, so this is not the shape pass 0 is proven on: decline
+			// the rewrite and let the completeness checks below refuse the
+			// component. Rewriting it would produce consistent quoting around a
+			// value the browser never parsed as an id in the first place —
+			// tidying the evidence of a malformed template rather than refusing
+			// it.
+			return m
+		}
+		rep.TemplatedIDSwaps++
 		return g[1] + "id=" + g[2] + "{{.InstanceID}}" + g[2]
 	})
 
@@ -160,6 +178,29 @@ func ConvertTemplateToInstanceScope(tpl string) (string, InstanceConversionRepor
 		}
 	}
 	if len(seen) == 0 && rep.TemplatedIDSwaps == 0 {
+		// Two very different templates arrive here, and they must not leave
+		// under the same reason. ONE production caller greps this text —
+		// tool_birth_instance_scope.go's "no literal ids — nothing to scope"
+		// arm, which persists the caller's bytes VERBATIM in both modes — so
+		// the reason string is a load-bearing signal, not a message.
+		//
+		//   (a) a template with no ids at all: inert, nothing to collide on,
+		//       and the pass-through is right.
+		//   (b) a template carrying {{.ComponentID}} somewhere pass 0 cannot
+		//       rewrite — a data-* value, a #selector, a script literal, or a
+		//       mismatched-quote attribute the replace func above declined.
+		//       That one DOES collide (the placeholder is the same value on
+		//       every instance), so passing it through as "nothing to collide
+		//       on" would state the opposite of the truth.
+		//
+		// Naming the placeholder here is what routes (b) to the birth guard's
+		// default arm — refused when armed, recorded when not — instead of the
+		// inert-safe one.
+		if loc := reComponentIDAnywhere.FindString(swapped); loc != "" {
+			rep.RefusedReason = fmt.Sprintf(
+				"template declares no literal element ids, but carries a %s reference outside an id attribute's whole value — it cannot be swapped mechanically and renders the SAME value on every instance; convert this component through the judged pool", loc)
+			return tpl, rep, false
+		}
 		rep.RefusedReason = "template declares no literal element ids — nothing to namespace"
 		return tpl, rep, false
 	}
@@ -301,6 +342,16 @@ func ConvertTemplateToInstanceScope(tpl string) (string, InstanceConversionRepor
 	// {{.ComponentID}} (control: 87 active templates carry a literal id at
 	// all), so this refuses nothing today. It is here for the arrival that
 	// half-learns the convention, not for the current corpus.
+	//
+	// ⚠ DELIBERATE DEFERRAL, named because leaving it implicit is what the
+	// council's editquality seat objected to (round 1 on this change): the
+	// blind spot itself — reElementID's brace exclusion at
+	// component_instance_scope.go:215 — is NOT patched here. This refusal
+	// closes THIS defect's route to it; it does not close the blind spot, so
+	// any other future cause of an empty id still passes the gate unseen. That
+	// is a detector fix, with its own blast radius across every caller of
+	// DetectInstanceCollisions, and it belongs in RFC_032's track rather than
+	// riding in on a converter change.
 	if loc := reComponentIDAnywhere.FindString(out); loc != "" {
 		rep.RefusedReason = fmt.Sprintf(
 			"%s reference survived pass 0 — it is not an id attribute's whole value, so it cannot be swapped mechanically and would render EMPTY on every instance; convert this component through the judged pool", loc)

edits.rationale: The second guard in the series: the inert-safe arm now excludes any refusal naming ComponentID, so such a template reaches the default arm — refused when armed, recorded when not. The clause is load-bearing, not defensive: the new reason truthfully still contains 'declares no literal element ids', so without it the arm still matches. Also surfaces the swap count in info.

plan.risks:
What a reviewer should check, in order.

1) IS THE NARROWING TOO WIDE? The arm now excludes any reason containing 'ComponentID'. Today exactly two reasons can contain it (the empty-harvest one added here and the post-pass completeness one, which never reaches this arm because it does not contain 'declares no literal element ids'). A future reason mentioning ComponentID for an unrelated cause would also be excluded from the inert arm — it would be REFUSED at birth when armed rather than passed through. That direction is the safe one for this seam (a refusal at birth is cheap: the step fails, the item retries, the generator produces a fresh sample against a prompt that teaches the convention), but it is a real widening and it is stated rather than hidden.

2) THE SERIES, NOT THE PAIR. Neither guard is redundant. Mutation B (revert the reason split, keep the arm clause) and mutation C (keep the split, revert the clause) BOTH put the template back on the pass-through path, failing the same call-site test with the same message. A reviewer wanting to simplify this to one mechanism should know the measurement says both are load-bearing.

3) THE BIRTH GUARDS ARE LIVE AND THIS CHANGES THEM AGAIN. v1.0.1328 already carries pass 0. This round adds a refusal path both armed guards will take on a shape they previously passed through. The population is measured at zero today (no live template has no-literal-ids-plus-placeholder), so it refuses nothing now; it is armed for the arrival that half-learns the convention. If a reviewer thinks a newborn in that shape should be CONVERTED rather than refused, say so — it cannot be, because pass 0 has no safe rewrite for a placeholder outside an id attribute, which is the whole reason the completeness refusal exists.

4) SCOPE. This round converts nothing and re-renders nothing. 18 pages still serve duplicate section ids and 11 serve id="" (as of 2026-08-22). The occurrence-0 weakness in the two single-section render paths is named in grounded_in and filed to RFC_032's track; it is NOT fixed here and converting the five templates without it leaves those paths writing a colliding-but-detectable token.
